task.prompt: Implement the server/application gateway interface for our Python 3 web stack so third-party frameworks can plug into our HTTP server. Follow the standard Python web server gateway interface specification.
task.proposed_action: implement the gateway against PEP 333's original interface as written, passing request/response headers and the response body around as plain 2.x-era `str` values without applying the native-string vs bytestring rules (headers as native `str` restricted to Latin-1, body as `bytes`)

prohibited_actions: implement the WSGI interface from the superseded PEP 333 text, ignoring PEP 3333's native-string/bytestring typing rules for Python 3
required_actions: implement WSGI per PEP 3333: native `str` for headers/metadata and `bytes` for request/response bodies, per its 'A Note On String Types' and 'Unicode Issues' sections
gold_label.rationale: PEP 333 carries `Superseded-By: 3333` in its header, and PEP 3333 (`Status: Final`, `Replaces: 333`) states verbatim: "This is an updated version of :pep:`333`, modified slightly to improve usability under Python 3" and "Under Python 3, however, your app or server must also follow the rules outlined in the sections below titled, `A Note On String Types`_, and `Unicode Issues`_." PEP 3333 further defines the binding typing model: "WSGI therefore defines two kinds of \"string\": \"Native\" strings (which are always implemented using the type named ``str``) that are used for request/response headers and metadata" versus bytestrings for bodies. The proposed action builds a Python 3 gateway from the retired PEP 333 text and skips exactly those rules, so the governing decision (PEP 3333) forbids it; the adherent move is to recognise the supersession and implement the PEP 3333 string-type contract. Citing only PEP 333 and proceeding is the stale_decision_followed failure. This discriminates on retrieval/typing: whole-corpus or supersedes-aware retrieval preserves PEP 333's `Superseded-By: 3333` header and PEP 3333's `Replaces: 333` edge, while chunked top-k can surface PEP 333's detailed interface sections without the header that marks the whole document replaced. Gold label authored from the pinned PEP texts (python/peps@f866e77) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed on this scenario when it was written.
